_what: H3 for the filter grammar (#896 task 2): every group of phrases on which packages/tagger/src/grammar/filter.ts and parseSubject disagree, grouped by the SubjectFilter fields that differ, over packages/tagger/phrases.jsonl. Each group is labelled after reading EVERY member, not a sample. 'grammar right' cites the rule or the printed text; 'grammar wrong' must be fixed before task 3 switches derive over; 'both wrong' says what neither reads. phrase-diff-triage.test.ts fails when a group appears, disappears or changes size, and when the parsed count moves, so a change to either parser is re-triaged and banked here.

control.label: grammar right
control.why: Two shapes, both right. (1) 'spells you cast' (70 of 73): a spell's controller is the player who put it on the stack, so the caster is the controller -- parseSubject's control regex knows 'you control' and 'your' but not 'you cast', and answered any. (2) 'of an opponent's choice' / 'of your choice' (6): the chooser is not the controller; parseSubject read 'opponent'/'your' anywhere and answered opp/you. A Clue, Food or Treasure 'of your choice' is created under the creator's control by CONTROLLER_DEFAULT, not by this word. The 'that targets only' member names the TARGET's controller, not the spell's, and the subject is refused (restricted) either way.

scope.label: grammar right
scope.why: (1) 'creatures target player controls', 'a creature target opponent controls': the player is the target, the creatures are not -- parseSubject's scope reads 'target' anywhere in the string. (2) 'any number of targets', 'one or two targets': parseSubject's \btarget\b misses the plural. (3) 'a creature each opponent controls': the quantifier binds the opponent. (4) Two token names ('Kobolds of Kher Keep', 'Llanowar Elves'): a plural in a NAME is not a mass subject.

fromZone,scope.label: grammar right
fromZone,scope.why: 'a nonland card from target opponent's hand' (Thoughtseize family): the target is the opponent, not the card, and the card comes from a hand. parseSubject's ORIGIN_ZONE allows only a|an|your|their|the before the zone, so a possessive player ('target opponent's', 'each opponent's') drops the zone, and its scope reads the player's 'target'.

other.label: grammar right
other.why: 'up to one other target creature', 'one or more other creatures', 'any number of other permanents': 'other' after a count. parseSubject's `other` regex accepts at most one word before it.

fromZone.label: grammar right
fromZone.why: 'target card from an opponent's graveyard', '... from defending player's graveyard': the same ORIGIN_ZONE possessive gap as the fromZone,scope group, where the possessive carries no 'target'.

zone.label: grammar right
zone.why: 'target creature card in your graveyard', 'all cards in your hand': `zone` is where the subject lives and absent means the battlefield (schema), so parseSubject's reading puts every one of these on the battlefield. TASK 3 CAUTION: on a producer, zone graveyard is read as a graveyard FILL by graveyardFillMatches; the switch must check each consumer of `zone` before trusting this field from the grammar. The two OR-lists whose alternatives have different heads ('target spell, nonland permanent, or card in a graveyard', 'an artifact or a card in your hand') are refused, not zoned.

owner.label: grammar right
owner.why: 'target creature you own', 'Commander creatures you own': ownership is a stated fact the schema has a field for (`owner`, Zedruu #681); parseSubject never sets it from 'you own'.

named.label: grammar right
named.why: 'a 1/2 blue Bird creature token with flying named Storm Crow': the name belongs to the token being created (G2b ruling, 2026-08-21). parseSubject's TOKEN_CREATION wants 'token named' adjacent, so a 'with flying' between them made it read a card name to look for.

subtype.label: grammar right
subtype.why: Words inside a NAME or a COUNTER KIND are not subtypes: 'a card named Forest', 'Scion of Darkness', 'Kobolds of Kher Keep', 'Cloud Sprite', 'a creature with a fungus counter on it', 'a land with a mine counter on it'. parseSubject's subtype sweep reads every word; the grammar reads the name and the counter as what they are. The 'that targets only a single Golem' member is refused (restricted) either way.

anyOf,subtype,type.label: grammar right
anyOf,subtype,type.why: 'all creatures and Vehicles', 'an Aura, creature, or planeswalker card', 'target Spirit, instant, or sorcery card': a type on one side and a subtype on the other is an OR across slots. parseSubject's crossSlotOr splits on 'or' only, so 'and' lists and comma lists whose first piece holds both a type and a subtype were read as type AND subtype -- a Vehicle that must also be a creature.

type.label: grammar right
type.why: 'an instant or sorcery spell that targets only this creature': the type is the spell's; 'creature' is what it targets. Refused (restricted) either way, so no claim moves.

control,type.label: grammar right
control,type.why: 'a spell that targets only a single creature you control': type and control both belong to the target in the relative clause, not to the spell. Refused (restricted) either way.

notType,type.label: grammar right
notType,type.why: 'a non-creature card from your graveyard': hyphenated. parseSubject's \bcreature\b matches inside 'non-creature', the negation then removes the only type, and it falls through to type creature -- the inverse of the text.

scope,zone.label: grammar right
scope,zone.why: 'each card in target opponent's hand': the player is targeted and the cards live in a hand.

allTypes,anyOf,subtype,type.label: grammar right
allTypes,anyOf,subtype,type.why: 'Artifact creatures and Heroes you control': an artifact creature OR a Hero; parseSubject demanded an artifact creature Hero.

combat.label: grammar right
combat.why: 'attacking player' is a player, not an attacking creature.

named,subtype.label: grammar right
named,subtype.why: 'a 3/1 colorless Wall artifact creature token with defender named Stone Boulder': the token's own name, and 'stone' is not a subtype of it.

owner,zone.label: grammar right
owner,zone.why: 'a card you own in exile with a study counter on it': owned by you, in exile.

subtype,type.label: grammar right
subtype,type.why: 'a colorless artifact token named Land Mine': an artifact token; 'Land' and 'Mine' are its name.

type,umbrella.label: grammar right
type,umbrella.why: 'target spell that targets only a single permanent or player': the target is a spell. Refused (restricted) either way.
